title: zazz script use cases
description: What agents and people do with zazz, step by step: an agent writes, tests, registers and calls a script; a developer installs a script and runs it as a command.

entities.name: Add a script and call it
entities.description: A coding agent writes a small program, tests it, registers it and calls it with JSON input.
entities.goal: Run a program it wrote, with a sandbox, from any directory, by an id that always means the same tested code.
preconditions: zazzled and zazz-worker are installed side by side; the agent runs `zazz` in a shell or uses `zazzled mcp`'s zazz tools.
For a Rust script, rustc with the wasm32-wasip1 target is installed.
The OS can sandbox processes: sandbox-exec on macOS, Landlock on Linux.
postconditions: The script's .wasm, precompiled .cwasm and metadata are in the registry under b3: and the BLAKE3 of the .zazz bytes; the .zazz itself is not kept.
The agent has the script's JSON output, and a warm worker is kept for the next call.

flow.action: Runs `zazz new NAME` (or zazz_new) and edits NAME/src/main.rs and NAME/tests/basic.rs.
Runs `zazz test NAME`; zazz packs the directory, builds it to WASM, AOT-compiles it and runs its tests in the sandbox, and replies with diagnostics or a test report, registering nothing.
Runs `zazz pack NAME` and gets the .zazz path and its id.
Reads the file once without following symlinks, ids it by BLAKE3 and, unless it is registered, takes the id's lock.

Checks any signature and takes a trust verdict, builds and tests in scratch space, then publishes the modules and metadata atomically and replies {hash, status: compiled, runtime, tests, warnings, signer, trusted}.
Runs `zazz call ID '{...}'` (or zazz_call with input, or an operation with params and body).
Resolves the id, builds the worker spec from the manifest and the verdict's grants, takes a warm worker or spawns one, and sends the call with the caller's streams (or capture pipes over MCP).
Relays progress until the result, returns the worker to the pool, and replies with the script's output (with captured stdout and stderr when there were any).

alternatives.condition: The script does not compile, or a test fails.
alternatives.outcome: build_failed with up to 20 condensed diagnostics, or tests_failed with the report; the agent fixes the code and tests again.

alternatives.condition: The same bytes are registered already.
alternatives.outcome: The reply has status cached and nothing is built.

alternatives.condition: A build or test fails, the signature does not verify, or the policy requires tests and there are none.
alternatives.outcome: An error reply (build_failed, tests_failed, invalid_signature, tests_missing); nothing is published.

alternatives.condition: The signer is not trusted here, or not for native code.
alternatives.outcome: The script is registered as an unsigned WASM script, with a warning saying so.

alternatives.condition: The id is unknown or ambiguous, or the OS cannot sandbox a WASM worker.
The call runs past its limit, the worker stops, or the caller hangs up.
alternatives.outcome: timeout, script_crashed or cancelled; the worker is killed rather than returned.

entities.name: Install a script and run it as a command
entities.description: A developer installs a .zazz under a name and runs it from a shell like any other command.
entities.goal: Use a script with flags, piped input and plain output, without knowing its id.
preconditions: zazzled, zazz-worker and the zazz invoker are installed side by side.
The developer has a .zazz file, or the id of a registered script.
postconditions: $ZAZZ_BIN (default ~/.zazzle/bin)/NAME links to the invoker and the registry maps NAME to the script.
Running NAME prints the script's output and exits with its code.

flow.action: Adds the file as zazz add does (or resolves an id), checks the name, records it and links the shim to the invoker; says to put the shim directory on PATH when it is not.
Runs `NAME ARGS...` in a shell, possibly with piped input.
Resolves NAME, parses the arguments with the manifest's cli spec (or passes {argv}), takes out --json.
Calls the script with mode human and the developer's own streams, showing progress on stderr.
Prints what the script returned as text, a table on a terminal or JSON, and exits with the script's code.

alternatives.condition: The name is invalid or reserved, the add fails, or a non-symlink file holds the shim's place.
alternatives.outcome: `zazz install: ...` with exit 1 or 2; no shim is made.

alternatives.condition: --help, or arguments the cli spec rejects.
alternatives.outcome: The generated usage with exit 0, or the parser's message with exit 2.

alternatives.condition: NAME is no longer installed or its script was removed.
The call fails or the script returns an error.
alternatives.outcome: `NAME: CODE: message`, exit 1 or the script's own code.
